title: Spectral point space of a quasi-compact stack with quasi-compact diagonal
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme, meaning a scheme isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Suppose $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact and its diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact, with both predicates as in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Give $|\mathcal X|$ the field-valued point set and smooth-atlas topology of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Then $|\mathcal X|$ is spectral [def-weil-spectral-space]: it is quasi-compact, the quasi-compact open subsets form a basis stable under finite intersections, and every nonempty irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point. No finite-type, Noetherian, separated-diagonal, or quasi-finite-diagonal hypothesis is imposed. The empty stack is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0DQN (lemma-spectral-qc-diagonal-qc), with affine base S: the proof uses an affine smooth atlas U and the affine product U times_S U. The affineness of S ensures this product is affine; no unrestricted-base variant is asserted.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-quasicompact-surjection] choose an affine smooth surjective atlas $a:A\to\mathcal X$. Its point map is continuous and surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Smoothness implies flatness and local finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open] makes $|a|$ open. The space $|A|$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], hence so is its continuous image $|\mathcal X|$. This last inference is the open-cover argument: pull an open cover back to $A$, choose a finite subcover, and use surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0DQN (lemma-spectral-qc-diagonal-qc), first paragraph, choice and openness of atlas

proof.text: Affine opens form a basis in $A$: cover any open subscheme by affine opens using [lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover]. For $x\in W\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ with $W$ open, choose a lift $v\in A$ of $x$ and an affine open $B\subseteq a^{-1}(W)$ containing $v$. The image $a(B)$ is open, contains $x$, and is contained in $W$; it is quasi-compact because $B$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and $a$ is continuous. Thus these images give a basis of quasi-compact opens. If $W$ itself is quasi-compact, finitely many such images cover $W$. The restrictions of $a$ to these affine opens are smooth, and their images correspond to open substacks by [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-open-image].

source.place: Tag 0DQN, first paragraph, quasi-compact open basis and finite lifts; schemes.tex Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens)

proof.text: Let $B,C\subseteq A$ be affine opens. Since $S$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $B\times_SC$ with an affine spectrum; it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Regard schemes as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. By [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], $R=B\times_{\mathcal X}C$ is an algebraic space. It is the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ by $B\times_SC\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ (an object is a pair with an isomorphism between its images). The definition [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] therefore gives a quasi-compact atlas of $R$. The continuous surjective point map of this atlas makes $|R|$ quasi-compact. Its image in $|\mathcal X|$ is exactly $a(B)\cap a(C)$: one inclusion follows from the two projections; for the other, equality of two field-point classes gives a common field extension and an isomorphism, hence an object of the $2$-fibre product. Consequently the intersection is quasi-compact. Express two arbitrary quasi-compact opens as finite unions of the images in step 2; distributing intersection over these finite unions proves their intersection quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0DQN, first paragraph, fibre-product argument; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian)

proof.text: Let $T\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ be nonempty, closed and irreducible. Construct its reduced closed substack without a field-base hypothesis. On the atlas $A$, give $D=a^{-1}(T)$ its unique reduced closed subscheme structure using [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Put $H=A\times_{\mathcal X}A$, with smooth projections $s,t$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The closed subspaces $s^{-1}D,t^{-1}D$ have equal support, since $as$ and $at$ are isomorphic. Each is reduced by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-reduced-locality], applied to its smooth map to $D$. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] gives equality as closed subspaces. Hence [lem-sfb-invariant-closed-substack-descent] supplies a closed algebraic substack $i:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$ with smooth surjective atlas $D$, so $\mathcal Z$ is reduced. The point map of $D\to\mathcal Z$ is surjective; its image in $\mathcal X$ is $T$ by the atlas closed-set criterion. By [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus], $|i|$ is a homeomorphism onto $T$.

For a full substack $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal X$ whose inclusion is a monomorphism, its diagonal is the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ to $\mathcal V\times_S\mathcal V$: over any test, its objects are precisely two objects of $\mathcal V$ and an isomorphism between them in $\mathcal X$, which by fullness is an isomorphism in $\mathcal V$. Thus $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$ is quasi-compact. Here stability of quasi-compactness under base change follows directly from [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]: a further quasi-compact test pulls back to the same fibre product with the original map. The inertia $I_{\mathcal Z/S}\to\mathcal Z$ is a base change of this diagonal, by its explicit object-and-automorphism description, so it too is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-qc-inertia-dense-open-gerbe] to obtain an open dense substack $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal Z$ and a gerbe $p:\mathcal U\to Q$ over an algebraic space. Since $T$ is nonempty, $|\mathcal U|$ is nonempty. The same diagonal base-change argument gives a quasi-compact $\Delta_{\mathcal U/S}$. No quasi-compactness of the dense open is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DQN, second and third paragraphs; Tag 06RC (proposition-open-stratum)

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism], $|p|:|\mathcal U|\to|Q|$ is a homeomorphism. By [lem-sfb-gerbe-qc-diagonal-descent], the relative diagonal of $Q/S$ is quasi-compact. The sobriety statement [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober] therefore applies to $Q$. Its point space is nonempty and irreducible: $|\mathcal U|$ is a nonempty open subset of the irreducible space $T$. Hence $|Q|$, considered as its own nonempty irreducible closed subset, has a unique generic point, and the homeomorphism gives a unique generic point $\eta$ of $|\mathcal U|$. This uses only sobriety of the quotient space, so it does not assume the dense open gerbe is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0DQN, final paragraph; Tag 0DQL; spaces-properties.tex Tag 06NJ (lemma-quasi-separated-sober)

proof.text: Since $|\mathcal U|$ is dense in $T$ and is the closure of $\eta$ in its subspace topology, $\overline{\{\eta\}}^{\,T}=T$. Any other generic point $\xi$ of $T$ lies in the nonempty open $|\mathcal U|$: otherwise its closed complement would contain $\xi$ and hence its closure $T$. Its closure inside $|\mathcal U|$ is then all of $|\mathcal U|$, so uniqueness there forces $\xi=\eta$. Thus every nonempty irreducible closed subset $T$ has a unique generic point. Together with steps 1–3, these are exactly the four conditions of [def-weil-spectral-space]. If $\mathcal X$ is empty, it is quasi-compact, the empty family is a compact-open basis, finite intersections are empty, and there are no nonempty irreducible closed subsets; the same conclusion holds.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DQN (lemma-spectral-qc-diagonal-qc); expanded reduced-support construction and topological generic-point argument. Sobriety alone (06NJ) suffices for the gerbe quotient, so it need not be quasi-compact.
